chips.definition: A number printed in a NASA technical standard, cited with its requirement ID (or table).

A number from a NASA technical report that is not a standard and has no requirement ID: an OCHMO technical brief or an HRP evidence report. NASA-authored, cited in full. (The source kind keeps its original name, nasa_brief.)
A number from NOAA's operational Space Weather Scales; not a NASA crew-health limit.
A number from a peer-reviewed paper or another public document (for example a NASA fact sheet or presentation), cited in full.
Arithmetic on published values; the inputs and the formula are shown.
No published basis: LANDFALL's own number, labeled as ours, with the reason.

categories.name: Fitness for Duty
categories.glossary: Minimum measurable capability or capacity for a given physiological or behavioral parameter that allows successful performance of all required duties.

categories.name: Space Permissible Exposure Limit
categories.shape: ceiling on cumulative exposure over a time window
categories.glossary: Quantifiable limit of exposure to a spaceflight factor over a given length of time, e.g., lifetime radiation exposure.

categories.name: Permissible Outcome Limit
categories.shape: maximum change against the crewmember's own pre-mission value
categories.glossary: Acceptable maximum decrement or change in a physiological or behavioral parameter, during or after a spaceflight mission, as the result of exposure to the space environment. Biological/clinical parameter measured, e.g., bone mineral density.

categories.name: Operational scale (other agency)
categories.shape: level on a published operational scale (NOAA S-scale)

categories.name: Personal reliable change (Tier B)
categories.shape: reliable change against the crewmember's own recent baseline (single-case t-test, Crawford & Howell 1998)

categories.name: Countermeasure target
categories.shape: a published countermeasure target that is not a NASA limit (the renal case's 24-h urine output, from the HRP renal stone evidence report); capped at caution

tiers.definition: A fixed number NASA or NOAA publishes: a NASA standard (with its requirement ID, or a Table 4.8-1 row and column), a NASA report without a requirement ID (the renal TARGET rule, from the HRP evidence report), or the NOAA S-scale. The chip says which. One Tier A rule, ops_onboard_proton_s3, reuses NOAA's S3 number at Mars, on the reading of a space-weather monitor in Mars orbit, where NOAA does not define its scale, so its chip is design choice.

Reliable change against the crewmember's own baseline: the single-case t-test of Crawford & Howell (1998), t = (value - baseline mean) / (baseline SD x sqrt(1 + 1/n)), df = n - 1, flagged when |t| exceeds the two-tailed critical value at alpha 0.001 (4.221 for a 14-day baseline). The idea of reliable change comes from Jacobson & Truax (1991); their arithmetic is not used. The test runs on the indicator's declared scale: counts (PVT-B lapses) on the Anscombe transform 2√(x + 3/8), with the band mapped back to the count.

severities.note: Exists in the type; LANDFALL never emits it. Emergency belongs to the vehicle caution and warning system.

source.rationale: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 Rev F Table 10.3-1 defines the alert classes (each row below quotes the definition of its class) and Appendix F Table F.5-1 their colours; which LANDFALL finding falls in which class is ours. The only Warning LANDFALL emits is a solar particle event at NOAA S3 or above, whose rules carry the shelter action (immediate action). FFD, PEL, POL and TARGET findings and Tier B changes need attention, not immediate action: Caution at most. LANDFALL never emits Emergency.

rows.class_definition: Event that needs attention, but not immediate action.
rows.note: A fitness-for-duty floor not met (VO2max below [V1 4001] or [V1 4002]: 'EVA fitness floor not met'), or an exposure or outcome limit reached, needs attention but not immediate action. Any immediate alarm (cabin CO2, suit CO2) belongs to the vehicle or suit caution and warning system. A Table 4.8-1 30-day blood-forming-organ dose over its limit also opens the shelter case, whose first steps are immediate; under this mapping that finding is still a Caution. Classing it as a Warning needs an engine change and is not in this build.

rows.class_definition: Event that needs attention, but not immediate action.
rows.note: At or past LANDFALL's watch level (80% of a ceiling, a design choice): needs attention before the limit.
Countermeasure targets (NASA report) are not NASA limits, so never warning (rule field max_severity).
rows.class_definition: Event that needs attention, but not immediate action.
Message describing a routine event, situation, or action, or an off-nominal event that does not meet the criteria for a Caution.

rows.note: Personal change is not a limit, so never warning.
rows.class_definition: Event that needs attention, but not immediate action.

rows.note: The direction opposite to the indicator's worse direction: shown, no alert. LANDFALL does not call it better.
A non-alerting indicator (mood, daytime light, skin temperature) shows its reliable change but never alerts: advisory blue would read as an alert. Missing data still shows as advisory (row no_data).

rows.class_definition: Message describing a routine event, situation, or action, or an off-nominal event that does not meet the criteria for a Caution.
Event that requires immediate action because it has the potential to become a life/mission threat.
rows.note: Every OPS rule at S3 or above carries the shelter action (action_id spe_shelter), which is immediate. In the same table, the Warning row's auditory annunciation gives 'Radiation' as an example warning message (Vol 2 Rev F, PDF page 206; the frozen snapshot keeps only the first clause of that column). An EVA in progress does not change the class.
[V2 10020]: indicate data that is stale, missing, unavailable, or unknown.
rows.colour_note: Severity advisory, but the colour is cyan, not advisory blue: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 Appendix F Table F.5-1 requires cyan for 'Missing or stale data'.

principles.text: NASA-STD-3001 publishes no numeric in-flight alert thresholds for crew health; its alert requirements leave the number to the program. LANDFALL never presents its own number as NASA's.
FFD (floor), PEL (ceiling on exposure over a window) and POL (maximum change from baseline) are never merged into one 'threshold exceeded' state.

refusals.text: No diagnosis. LANDFALL reports measurements against published limits and your own baseline; diagnosis is a flight surgeon's job.
No medication or dosing advice to the crew; medication decisions belong to the flight surgeon.
No psychiatric alert. Mood is private, never alerts, and leaves the device only with consent.
No personal cancer-risk (REID) model. NASA's 600 mSv career limit uses 35-year-old female model parameters for everyone ([V1 4030] note).
No claim that CO2 causes a cognitive deficit; the defensible claim is headache risk.
LANDFALL never raises an Emergency-class alarm; that belongs to the vehicle caution and warning system.
LANDFALL is not the radiation alarm: the vehicle's radiation monitoring system raises it ([V2 6164]); LANDFALL opens the health case that follows and guides the crew.
No radiation dose projection of our own; LANDFALL triggers on NOAA's scale near Earth or on the Mars-orbit space-weather monitor at Mars.
No language model in the decision path; every rule is data you can read on /provenance.

backup.label: Second Crew Medical Officer: the Commander (onboard)
backup.name: the Commander
backup.role_text: the crew's second Crew Medical Officer
backup.applies: when the patient is the Crew Medical Officer

source.rationale: NASA-STD-3001 requires at least two Crew Medical Officers per vehicle. [V1 3006] reads 'The program(s) shall train a minimum of two crewmembers per vehicle/platform as Crew Medical Officers (CMOs).', and its rationale gives the reason: 'to ensure that a backup is available for medical treatment'. When the Crew Medical Officer (CM-4) is the patient, tier 1 goes to the crew's second Crew Medical Officer. In the demo crew the Commander (CM-1) holds that second assignment; which crewmember holds it is LANDFALL's choice, not a NASA assignment. LANDFALL does not assume either Crew Medical Officer is a physician: its texts are written so a non-physician can act, as [V2 7045] asks of medical equipment 'in the event that a physician crewmember is not present or is the one who requires medical treatment'.

citations.verbatim: in the event that a physician crewmember is not present or is the one who requires medical treatment
The program(s) shall train a minimum of two crewmembers per vehicle/platform as Crew Medical Officers (CMOs).
to ensure that a backup is available for medical treatment

tiers.label: Flight surgeon (ground)
tiers.name: the flight surgeon
tiers.when: through the ground packet, with the next link: at once when the link is up (AOS), when it resumes during loss of signal or solar conjunction

autonomy.AOS: With the link up (for example at the ISS, in cislunar space or on the lunar surface), the ground has the case within the round-trip light time; the crew follows Mission Control and flight-surgeon direction, and LANDFALL is the decision aid.
autonomy.LOS: With no link (loss of signal or solar conjunction), the crew acts onboard with its Crew Medical Officers; the ground packet stays Prepared (held on board) until the crew releases it or the case escalates, then it is Queued and sent when the link resumes.

source.rationale: Earth-independent operations put the onboard Crew Medical Officer first, and the flight surgeon is reached through the ground packet. How much the crew decides onboard scales with the link, as [V2 6164]'s rationale does for radiation alerts: the crew is alerted even when ground communication is unviable, and operations teams when communication is available or restored.

citations.verbatim: The crew must be alerted even if ground communication is disrupted or is unviable.
The systems must alert operations teams if communication is available or upon being restored.

packet_states.label: Prepared (held on board)
packet_states.when: the case is open and the packet has been neither released by the crew nor escalated: it is built on board and not sent

packet_states.label: Queued
packet_states.when: after crew release (a procedure step that releases the packet) or escalation: it is sent when a link exists, at once at AOS, when the link resumes during loss of signal or solar conjunction

body_region_rule: A case's body_regions are its hazard footprint, the organs the hazard can reach, drawn as a hatched outline. Only a measured finding for the selected crewmember fills an organ. VO2max is a fitness tag (EVA assignment), not a heart or lung finding.
